column1:
Maintaining the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50% and signaling “patience” aligns with rule-like policy behavior (Taylor-rule/Rudebusch) and inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson), given muted inflation and low market-based inflation compensation. Tight labor markets need not produce immediate inflation pressure (hybrid Phillips curve; wage-contract rigidity), supporting a pause. The symmetric 2% objective reinforces credibility and helps limit inflation bias, while softer household spending and business investment argue against further near-term tightening.

FSR lens: The Financial Stability Report highlights financial stability concerns reported by the New York Fed and relies on market-based indicators (e.g., similar-maturity Treasury yields; Barclays/Refinitiv/Thomson Reuters data) that have shown low inflation compensation and periods of compressed risk premia. This stability assessment strengthens the case for patience to avoid adding to vulnerabilities or amplifying financial accelerator dynamics. Net tone: modestly dovish, with a stability-aware tilt.
